subject.title: Dashboard shows deployment version drift warning

question: Should ClawHub treat frontend/Convex SHA mismatch as an actionable production error, or should expected backend-only and frontend-only deploys downgrade or suppress this dashboard warning?
rationale: The source path is working as currently tested, and changing it without maintainer intent could either hide real skew or keep a red warning for expected partial deploys.

options.title: Keep Strict Same-SHA Warning
options.body: Treat the red warning as correct when SHAs differ, and fix deployment stamping or release ordering when production drifts.

options.title: Downgrade Expected Partial Drift
options.body: If partial deploy targets are normal, make the banner copy/severity distinguish expected partial drift from actionable skew and update tests/docs together.

options.title: Disable Drift Detection
options.body: Suppressing the check would remove noisy warnings but would also lose the signal that catches real frontend/backend deployment skew.

recommendation.title: Keep Strict Same-SHA Warning
recommendation.body: Treat the red warning as correct when SHAs differ, and fix deployment stamping or release ordering when production drifts.

likelyOwner.reason: The central banner, metadata query, deploy workflow, and deploy runbook blame to Patrick-Erichsen in current history.
